reader.decision: Approve `cache: pnpm` on `actions/setup-node@v4` as the change to show the team, and present the 8 min 00 s figure as an estimate until a real cached run confirms it.
reader.decision_reason: The change is one added line in `ci.yml`, it uses the built-in lockfile-hash key, and the cost and failure modes are small and stated. The only gap is that the warm-store number is unconfirmed, which labelling it as an estimate handles.

reconstruction.problem: Every CI run of `fernway-web` re-downloads the whole 1.1 GB pnpm store, because `actions/setup-node@v4` caches nothing. The median `Install` step takes 3 min 40 s, so about 3 min 05 s of each run goes on re-downloading unchanged packages. The run total is 11 min 05 s, and week 43 had 412 runs.
reconstruction.what_breaks: Nothing is broken. The cost is waste: about 1,270 minutes, roughly 21 runner-hours and 10 USD per week, plus developers waiting about 3 min longer per run.
reconstruction.fix: Add `cache: pnpm` under `with:` of the `actions/setup-node@v4` step in `.github/workflows/ci.yml`. The step already runs after `pnpm/action-setup@v4`, which the option requires. The cache key is the `pnpm-lock.yaml` hash. The median install should drop to about 35 s and the run total to about 8 min 00 s. The alternative is `actions/cache` with an explicit key and `restore-keys`, at about six more lines.
reconstruction.cost: Each lockfile change writes a new cache entry of up to 1.1 GB uncompressed, against a 10 GB repository limit, and the oldest entries are evicted first. A cold run after a lockfile change is no faster than today, and the cache adds restore and save time. The 35 s figure comes from 20 manual runs and may not include restore time. The lockfile path was not checked.

reader.closing_answer: Yes, I approve `cache: pnpm` on `actions/setup-node@v4` as the change to show the team. Label 8 min 00 s as an estimate, and keep `actions/cache` with `restore-keys` as the fallback if cold runs after lockfile changes hurt.
